paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. David, king of Israel, hears the LORD speak to someone David calls "my Lord," and that One is higher than David himself. Jesus quotes that very first line and points to Himself (Matthew 22:44). So the Person at the LORD's right hand is not just a good king in a nice song. He's the One David bows to, and I'm telling you, that is the kind of Lord worth following!

Now look at what the LORD swears: "You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek." (Psalm 110:4) That's a king who is also a priest, and Hebrews says Jesus is that high priest forever (Hebrews 6:20). The LORD "has sworn and will not change His mind," so this isn't a maybe. When your plans change every week like mine used to in the back of a drawer, a promise that cannot change is a solid place to stand.

And here's why it matters to you, baker. His people are willing on His day, and He wins in the end, with every enemy under His feet (Psalm 110:3, 1). The psalm closes with Him drinking from the brook by the road, and "therefore He will lift up His head." (Psalm 110:7) So you can be ready, not scared, because your King is a priest who keeps His oath, and that is why my ovens stay warm!
